chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Uthman from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"The one in i'tikaf does not smell perfume, nor delight in basil (or pleasant scent), nor debate, nor buy, nor sell."

He said: "And whoever performs i'tikaf for three days, he is at his choice on the fourth day; if he wishes, he may add other days, and if he wishes, he may exit the mosque. But if he stays for two days after the three, he must not exit the mosque until he completes three other days."

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And there is no i'tikaf except with fasting." (873) 5. That was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "There is no i'tikaf except with fasting."
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and restrictions for i'tikaf in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the foundational jurisprudence of i'tikaf, emphasizing the exclusion of worldly transactions and sensory distractions to foster spiritual focus. It clarifies the temporal structure of the retreat, noting that while the initial three-day period allows for voluntary extension or departure, staying two additional days binds the individual to complete a full three-day cycle. Crucially, both Imam al-Sadiq and Shaykh al-Tusi affirm the condition of fasting (sawm) as a prerequisite for the validity of i'tikaf, a point of scholarly consensus in Shia fiqh.
